non_rust_exception_baseline._comment: FROZEN review-visible baseline of TODAY's accepted temporary_legacy_bridge non-Rust automation exceptions (the exceptions[] allowlist). The file-extension scan permits a non-Rust file iff it has an exceptions[] entry (any-allowlisted-ok); this dimension additionally freezes that EXCEPTION SET shrink-only so a NEW .py/.sh bridge cannot be admitted by silently adding an allowlist row. A current exception NOT in this baseline is born-blocking (rust_first_automation_unbaselined_non_rust_exception) -- convert it to owned Rust (e.g. a contract-slice entry on //ci/facade/contract-slice-conformance) rather than shell/Python; a removed bridge must shrink this baseline in the SAME PR (rust_first_automation_non_rust_exception_baseline_stale). Folded INTO this policy (zero new tracked accounting rows); NOT producer-regenerated -- reviewed, hand-shrunk; anti-laundering is REVIEW-VISIBLE: growing the bridge set now requires an explicit reviewed baseline edit, not a routine-looking allowlist append.

_provenance.policy: shrink-only; growth requires a review-visible baseline edit, retirement must shrink in the same PR

product_contract.ci_hygiene: The scanner is read-only, creates no temporary files, and detects stale exceptions so policy debt cleans up after retired files.
product_contract.cloud_native: Exceptions must point toward Rust cloud-ci, Kubernetes, GitOps, controller, or admission-policy replacements; new infrastructure packages must be app/gate/controller/API-shaped, not CLI-shaped.
product_contract.execution: Buck2-native Rust gate; no Cargo command is required for enforcement.
product_contract.portability: Policy is data-driven so another repository can adopt the same gate by changing scan roots and exceptions.

purpose: Rust-first automation hygiene ratchet. Non-Rust scripts are blocked unless explicitly exceptioned as shrinkable debt with a Rust/Buck2/cloud-native replacement path; cloud/infra/tooling CLI-first package births are blocked outright.

cli_package_authority._comment: Cloud-native infrastructure automation must not be born as a new CLI-first package. This dimension scans infrastructure/cloud/tooling Cargo manifests for package names with retired CLI suffixes. Existing product/local legacy CLIs outside these roots remain governed by their own retirement lanes; new cloud/infra/tooling work should be an app, gate, controller, service, API, or declarative config consumer instead.

interpreter_command_authority._comment: G006 inventory-first guard: Rust automation/gate source must not re-authorize retired Python/Node/MJS authority by spawning interpreter commands directly. The scan is intentionally scoped to automation/gate code; cloud/cloud-os is owned by the later kernel/OS story and is excluded from this task-4 lane.

workflow_forbidden_uses._comment: Forbid third-party / marketplace Buck2 setup actions. The allowed bridge is repo-owned infra/ci/install-buck2.sh, which downloads the official facebook/buck2 release asset and verifies the pinned SHA-256 before execution.

workflow_inline_shell._comment: pipeline-glue(a): the file-extension scan above is blind to shell that lives INSIDE workflow YAML `run:` steps (the file is `.yml`, not `.sh`). This dimension parses the declared workflow roots with a real YAML parser, emits one schema-v2 keyed observation per (file, job, required unique run-step name) with exact non-empty shell_lines, and ratchets it against the embedded workflow_inline_shell_baseline. New keys or line-count growth are born-blocking; retired keys or line-count shrink must shrink the baseline in the same PR. Missing or duplicate names fail closed. Removing the shell itself (productizing it as a Rust/Buck2 step) is pipeline-glue(b).

workflow_inline_shell_baseline._comment: FROZEN exact named-step baseline of accepted workflow inline shell. Each entry is {key, shell_lines}, keyed as <workflow-relpath>::<job-id>::<required unique run-step name>. Both the named key set and shell_lines are exact shrink-accounted: a new key or line-count growth is born-blocking; a removed key or line-count shrink makes this baseline stale until it shrinks in the same reviewed PR. Missing or duplicate run-step names and malformed or duplicate baseline rows fail closed. This schema-v2 baseline was mechanically migrated from exact origin/dev commit 30dd46c4dd7d12c085b77332d9ac5035d583edcf, preserving its accepted 58 workflow run steps and measured non-empty shell line counts.

_provenance.authority: pipeline-glue(a): rust-first ratchet workflow-inline-shell go-live; door:one-way
_provenance.buck2_required_ci_note: 2026-06-25 #839: the required CI bridge is Buck2-only. The gate matrix adds one reviewed inline-shell key for the repo-owned official-Buck2 installer plus the Buck2 test step (gate::step-2..4). The live-Postgres lanes replace Swatinem rust-cache and cargo test with repo-owned install-buck2, actions/cache toolchain warmup, and buck2 test --local-only against isolated Postgres services; #901 splits the accepted live-Postgres keys into adapter/facade jobs (step-1 and step-3..6 for each lane). This remains transitional runner glue until the owned cloud-ci runner models the disposable database as a managed local_resource.
_provenance.fric_017_note: FRIC-017 disk-reclaim run-blocks are PRODUCTIZED in pipeline-glue(b): each former multi-line sudo rm -rf block is now a build-as-user + sudo-binary invocation of the data-driven Rust preflight oya-cloud-ci-runner-disk-reclaim-bin. Schema-v1 positional identities were historical only; schema-v2 records the required named run-step key and exact shell_lines, so any later footprint shrink must update this frozen baseline in the same reviewed PR.
_provenance.migration: v1 positional step-N keys migrated mechanically from exact origin/dev base to required unique named-step keys with measured shell_lines; v2 is exact shrink-accounted.
